"# LOST SIGNAL: OUTPOST 09
## A Lightweight 3D Sci-Fi Exploration Game

Create a visually impressive, fully playable 3D sci-fi exploration game called LOST SIGNAL: OUTPOST 09.

IMPORTANT: This is a performance-conscious 3D game prototype. It must look atmospheric and detailed while remaining lightweight enough to run smoothly on mid-range Android phones and desktop browsers.

Do not create a 2D game. Use genuine real-time 3D rendering.

## 1. GAME CONCEPT

The player is an exploration specialist sent to investigate an abandoned futuristic research outpost.

The facility contains valuable technology, abandoned equipment, mysterious signals and autonomous security robots.

The player must explore the facility, collect valuable objects, avoid security robots and reach the extraction point.

Create a compact but immersive gameplay experience.

## 2. GRAPHICS AND ART STYLE

Use Three.js or another lightweight browser-based 3D engine.

Visual style:
- Stylized realistic 3D.
- High-quality low-poly models.
- Futuristic industrial architecture.
- Dark metallic surfaces.
- Cyan and orange illuminated details.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Carefully placed lights.
- Subtle shadows.
- Glowing computer terminals.
- Detailed environmental props.

The game should look like a small indie sci-fi game, not a primitive demonstration.

Use attractive materials and thoughtful environmental composition instead of expensive graphics effects.

## 3. ENVIRONMENT

Create ONE compact but detailed 3D research facility.

Include:
- A central laboratory.
- Two interconnected corridors.
- A storage room.
- A small maintenance area.
- A locked research room.
- One extraction platform.

Add:
- Metal doors.
- Storage containers.
- Desks and computer terminals.
- Pipes and machinery.
- Warning lights.
- Abandoned equipment.
- Environmental details.

Use modular geometry and reusable objects.

Do not generate a huge open world.

## 4. PLAYER CHARACTER

Create a recognizable 3D futuristic exploration operative.

Appearance:
- Dark exploration suit.
- Compact backpack.
- Helmet.
- Cyan glowing visor.
- Small illuminated suit details.

Use simple but smooth animations:
- Idle.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Turning.

Use a third-person camera positioned behind the character.

The camera should smoothly follow the player and allow rotation.

## 5. MOVEMENT AND CONTROLS

Desktop:
- WASD: movement.
- Mouse: camera rotation.
- Shift: sprint.
- E: interact.
- Tab: inventory.
- Escape: pause.

Mobile:
- Virtual joystick on the left.
- Camera control on the right.
- Interaction button.
- Sprint button.
- Inventory button.

Make touch controls responsive and comfortable.

Implement proper collision detection.

Prevent the player from walking through walls and objects.

## 6. ENEMY AI

Add TWO autonomous security robots.

They should:
- Patrol predefined areas.
- Detect the player when nearby and visible.
- Investigate suspicious activity.
- Chase the player after detection.
- Search the area after losing sight.
- Eventually return to patrol.

Make their behavior believable and lightweight.

Do not use complicated machine-learning systems.

Implement enemy behavior with efficient finite-state machines.

## 7. STEALTH SYSTEM

Allow the player to:
- Hide behind designated objects.
- Break enemy line of sight.
- Move away from detected enemies.
- Use a hide interaction button.

While hiding:
- Make the player visually less noticeable.
- Prevent movement only when the player is actively using a fixed hiding spot.
- Allow the player to leave hiding normally.

Enemies must not magically track invisible players.

## 8. LOOT AND INTERACTION

Place several collectible objects throughout the facility.

Include:
- Electronic components.
- Energy cells.
- Research documents.
- Rare technology modules.

Give each item:
- A recognizable 3D model.
- A name.
- A rarity.
- A pickup notification.

Use a small inventory with six slots.

Add interactive storage containers and computer terminals.

## 9. EXTRACTION

Create one clearly visible extraction point.

The player must collect at least three research items before extraction becomes available.

When the player reaches the extraction point:
- Display an interaction prompt.
- Start a short extraction countdown.
- Show extraction progress.
- Display a mission completion screen.

Show recovered items and earned credits.

## 10. USER INTERFACE

Create a polished dark sci-fi HUD.

Display:
- Health.
- Energy.
- Battery.
- Inventory capacity.
- Current objective.
- Interaction prompts.
- Extraction status.

Add a pause menu and mission completion screen.

Keep the interface readable on mobile screens.

## 11. AUDIO

If lightweight audio is available, include:
- Ambient laboratory sounds.
- Electronic interface sounds.
- Footsteps.
- Robot movement sounds.
- Warning signals.

Audio must be optional and must never prevent the game from running.

## 12. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

These requirements are critical:

- Target smooth performance on mid-range Android devices.
- Use low-poly geometry.
- Keep texture resolution small.
- Use a limited number of real-time lights.
- Avoid expensive post-processing.
- Avoid real-time global illumination.
- Use simple shadows or baked-looking lighting.
- Keep the number of active objects reasonable.
- Reuse geometry and materials.
- Use efficient collision detection.
- Avoid unnecessary background processing.
- Keep memory usage low.
- Include a graphics quality setting if practical.

Do not load large external assets.

Generate simple 3D models procedurally when necessary.

## 13. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Use a browser-compatible 3D engine.
- Prefer Three.js.
- Use WebGL.
- Make the game playable directly in the browser.
- Do not require external APIs or paid services.
- Do not require an account or server connection during gameplay.
- Make all controls functional.
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
- Organize files efficiently.
- Ensure the project builds successfully.

## 14. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITY

First create a working playable version containing:

1. A 3D environment.
2. A recognizable player character.
3. Third-person camera.
4. Responsive movement.
5. Collision detection.
6. Two working enemy robots.
7. Collectible objects.
8. A functional extraction point.
9. Mobile controls.

Only after these features work, improve visual details and animations.

Do not implement decorative features that do not work.

Do not create a large unfinished game.

The final result should be a compact, atmospheric and genuinely enjoyable 3D sci-fi game that demonstrates excellent visual quality without requiring powerful hardware.

Most importantly: BUILD A WORKING GAME, NOT JUST A BEAUTIFUL SCREENSHOT.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

content.text: Created file successfully: src/world/outpost.js

Need to check props.crate rotation = 0.2 non-axis: collider still size; okay. But cart at 7.7,2.3 size1.3 anchor y 1.3 correct (height 1.196).
CrateStack at 2.6,-26 rot 0.2 gives colliders axis aligned fine.

Potential issue props.locker front direction/hidePos: for rot=0 front +Z; for rot=-PI/2 front -X. hidePos at x + fx2*.35, z + fz2*.35. For locker at (10.2,7.0), rot=-PI/2: hidePos x=9.85,z=7.0; camera inside/at front. Player hidden. Fine.

But hide spot interaction position uses x + fx2*.65, z + fz2*.65; for locker at 10.2 => 9.55, fine.

World floor texture generation: each floorTexture gets 256 canvas; 8 textures ~2MB. Good.

Now player.js: character model + animation + movement/camera controller? Split player character model and player controller.

Character: `createOperative(THREE)` returns group with userData parts. Build with low-poly capsules/boxes.

Design:
- Root group. Character height 1.82.
- pelvis at y=0.95, torso from 0.95 to 1.5; chest armor.
- head at 1.63, helmet sphere/capsule with visor front (local +Z? We need know facing). Player movement uses group.rotation.y = yaw where yaw=atan2(dx,dz) so local +Z points movement direction. Mesh front should be +Z. Visor at z+0.15.
- backpack at z-0.18.
- arms with pivot at shoulders y1.42, x±0.32; upper arm boxes/capsules down; forearms. Animate rotation.x swing.
- legs pivot at hip y0.9 x±0.14; thigh, shin, boot. Animate.
- cyan strips: chest, shoulders, boots, helmet sides, backpack.
- suit dark #1a2630, armor #2a3a45, orange accents small.
- visor cyan emissive with glow sprite maybe. Use MeshBasicMaterial.
- antenna? small.
- shoulder pad.
- helmet a `SphereGeometry` scaled or CapsuleGeometry. Use `SphereGeometry(0.2,10,8)` scaled (1,1.1,1.05), dark; visor a curved plane? Use BoxGeometry(0.28,0.11,0.04) at z .19, plus a smaller strip.
- backpack box (0.34,0.42,0.18) with cyan strips, pipes.

Animation:
- idle: root bob, chest breathing; arms subtle; head.
- walk: leg swing sin(phase)*0.55, arms opposite; body bob; backpack.
- run: bigger swing, lean.
- turning: smooth rotation to movement direction; maybe tilt when turning. Player root rotates with damp.
- when airborne? no jump.
- crouch hidden crates: scale? set model group scale y=.75 and maybe position y=0; hidden locker hide mesh.

Player controller:
- position Vector3 (start x, z=6.4), radius .38, speed walk 3.3, sprint 5.7.
- energy 100; sprint drains 18/s, regen 12/s; battery 100 (flashlight 6/s, regen? no; battery pickups refill). Flashlight off drains none. Health 100.
- input state from main: move vector (x,z normalized), sprint bool, camera yaw.
- `update(dt, input, cameraYaw, world, paused)`:
  - if hidden: no movement, animate idle crouched; position fixed; mesh handling.
  - desired direction relative camera: forward = (-sin(yaw), -cos(yaw))? Need camera coordinate convention.

Camera orbit yaw: camera positioned behind player at angle yaw. Define yaw=0 means camera behind looking toward -Z? Let's define camera offset:

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D sci-fi exploration game "LOST SIGNAL: OUTPOST 09" in the current Vite + Three.js project, with a compact detailed facility, third-person character, stealth robots, loot, extraction, HUD, mobile controls, and audio.
- Performance-conscious for mid-range Android and desktop; genuine WebGL 3D, no external/paid assets or APIs.

## Requirements
- Use Three.js/WebGL, browser-playable, buildable project; avoid heavy post-processing and large assets.
- One facility with central lab, two corridors, storage, maintenance, locked research room, extraction platform.
- Procedural player operative (dark suit, helmet, cyan visor, backpack) with idle/walk/run/turn animation and third-person camera.
- WASD, mouse look, Shift sprint, E interact, Tab inventory, Escape pause; mobile joystick, look drag, interact/sprint/inventory.
- Collision detection; two FSM security robots with patrol/detect/investigate/chase/search/return; hiding spots that block enemy detection.
- Collectibles with 3D models, names, rarity, pickup notifications; 6-slot inventory; interactive containers/terminals; 3 research items required; extraction countdown + mission complete screen with credits.
- HUD: health, energy, battery, inventory capacity, objective, prompts, extraction status; pause, mission complete, mobile-readable.
- Optional lightweight audio (ambient, UI, footsteps, robot/warning).
- Procedural geometry, shared materials, capped pixel ratio, limited lights/shadows, quality setting.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; note assumptions at finish.

## Decisions
- Built from scratch as Vite 7 + three 0.180.0, all geometry/materials/audio procedural; no external assets.
- Layout rooms: lab (22×18), storage (16×12 north), maintenance (12×14 east), locked research (12×10 west), extraction bay south, north/east/south corridors.
- Static geometry merged per material via BufferGeometryUtils Batch; props share materials; 6 point lights + hemisphere + directional shadow light; shadows disabled on low.
- Two hover security sentinels K-7 (lab) and K-9 (storage/corridor), FSM + vision cone + segment-AABB LOS.
- Inventory 6 slots, drop supported; research items are Voss log, Signal Analysis, Quantum Core; keycard is separate quest flag, not a slot.
- Hiding uses first-person concealed camera (player model hidden) for lockers and crate nooks.

734: function updateJoystick(clientX, clientY) {
735:   const rect = joyEl.getBoundingClientRect()
736:   const cx = rect.left + rect.width / 2
737:   const cy = rect.top + rect.height / 2
738:   const max = rect.width * 0.32
739:   let dx = clientX - cx
740:   let dy = clientY - cy
741:   const len = Math.hypot(dx, dy)
742:   if (len > max) { dx = dx / len * max; dy = dy / len * max }
743:   joystick.x = dx / max
744:   joystick.z = -dy / max
745:   joyStick.style.transform = `translate(${dx}px, ${dy}px)`
746:   joyEl.classList.add('active')
747: }

750:   e.preventDefault()
751:   if (state !== 'playing') return
752:   joystick.pointerId = e.pointerId
753:   joyEl.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)
754:   updateJoystick(e.clientX, e.clientY)
755: })
756: joyEl.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
757:   if (joystick.pointerId !== e.pointerId) return
758:   e.preventDefault()

761: function endJoystick(e) {
762:   if (joystick.pointerId !== e.pointerId) return
763:   joystick.pointerId = null
764:   joystick.x = 0
765:   joystick.z = 0
766:   joyStick.style.transform = 'translate(0px, 0px)'
767:   joyEl.classList.remove('active')
768: }
769: joyEl.addEventListener('pointerup', endJoystick)
770: joyEl.addEventListener('pointercancel', endJoystick)
771: joyEl.addEventListener('pointerleave', (e) => { if (joystick.pointerId === e.pointerId) endJoystick(e) })

907: function getInput() {
908:   let x = 0, z = 0
909:   if (keys.has('KeyA') || keys.has('ArrowLeft')) x -= 1
910:   if (keys.has('KeyD') || keys.has('ArrowRight')) x += 1
911:   if (keys.has('KeyW') || keys.has('ArrowUp')) z += 1
912:   if (keys.has('KeyS') || keys.has('ArrowDown')) z -= 1
913:   if (Math.hypot(joystick.x, joystick.z) > 0.12) {
914:     x = joystick.x
915:     z = joystick.z
916:   }
917:   const len = Math.hypot(x, z)
918:   if (len > 1) { x /= len; z /= len }
919:   input.x = x
920:   input.z = z
921:   input.sprint = keys.has('ShiftLeft') || keys.has('ShiftRight') || mobileSprint
922:   return input
923: }

925: function updateCamera(dt) {
926:   if (player.hidden) {
927:     const eye = player.hideType === 'locker' ? 1.53 : 1.08
928:     const p = player.position
929:     const shake = cam.shake
930:     camera.position.set(
931:       p.x + (Math.random() - 0.5) * shake,
932:       eye + (Math.random() - 0.5) * shake,
933:       p.z + (Math.random() - 0.5) * shake,
934:     )
935:     const pitch = Math.max(-0.55, Math.min(0.55, cam.pitch))
936:     camera.rotation.set(-pitch, cam.yaw, 0)
937:     cam.shake *= Math.exp(-dt * 9)
938:   } else {
939:     cam.update(dt, player, world, false, null)
940:   }
941: }

949: function simulationStep(dt) {
950:   elapsed += dt
951:   const inp = getInput()
952:   player.update(dt, inp, cam.yaw, world, state === 'playing')
953:   world.update(dt, player.position, robots)
954:   loot.update(dt, elapsed)
955:   for (const r of robots) r.update(dt, player, world, true)
956:   updateCamera(dt)
957:   updateExtraction(dt)

messages.text:
"# LOST SIGNAL: OUTPOST 09
## A Lightweight 3D Sci-Fi Exploration Game

Create a visually impressive, fully playable 3D sci-fi exploration game called LOST SIGNAL: OUTPOST 09.

IMPORTANT: This is a performance-conscious 3D game prototype. It must look atmospheric and detailed while remaining lightweight enough to run smoothly on mid-range Android phones and desktop browsers.

Do not create a 2D game. Use genuine real-time 3D rendering.

## 1. GAME CONCEPT

The player is an exploration specialist sent to investigate an abandoned futuristic research outpost.

The facility contains valuable technology, abandoned equipment, mysterious signals and autonomous security robots.

The player must explore the facility, collect valuable objects, avoid security robots and reach the extraction point.

Create a compact but immersive gameplay experience.

## 2. GRAPHICS AND ART STYLE

Use Three.js or another lightweight browser-based 3D engine.

Visual style:
- Stylized realistic 3D.
- High-quality low-poly models.
- Futuristic industrial architecture.
- Dark metallic surfaces.
- Cyan and orange illuminated details.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Carefully placed lights.
- Subtle shadows.
- Glowing computer terminals.
- Detailed environmental props.

The game should look like a small indie sci-fi game, not a primitive demonstration.

Use attractive materials and thoughtful environmental composition instead of expensive graphics effects.

## 3. ENVIRONMENT

Create ONE compact but detailed 3D research facility.

Include:
- A central laboratory.
- Two interconnected corridors.
- A storage room.
- A small maintenance area.
- A locked research room.
- One extraction platform.

Add:
- Metal doors.
- Storage containers.
- Desks and computer terminals.
- Pipes and machinery.
- Warning lights.
- Abandoned equipment.
- Environmental details.

Use modular geometry and reusable objects.

Do not generate a huge open world.

## 4. PLAYER CHARACTER

Create a recognizable 3D futuristic exploration operative.

Appearance:
- Dark exploration suit.
- Compact backpack.
- Helmet.
- Cyan glowing visor.
- Small illuminated suit details.

Use simple but smooth animations:
- Idle.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Turning.

Use a third-person camera positioned behind the character.

The camera should smoothly follow the player and allow rotation.

## 5. MOVEMENT AND CONTROLS

Desktop:
- WASD: movement.
- Mouse: camera rotation.
- Shift: sprint.
- E: interact.
- Tab: inventory.
- Escape: pause.

Mobile:
- Virtual joystick on the left.
- Camera control on the right.
- Interaction button.
- Sprint button.
- Inventory button.

Make touch controls responsive and comfortable.

Implement proper collision detection.

Prevent the player from walking through walls and objects.

## 6. ENEMY AI

Add TWO autonomous security robots.

They should:
- Patrol predefined areas.
- Detect the player when nearby and visible.
- Investigate suspicious activity.
- Chase the player after detection.
- Search the area after losing sight.
- Eventually return to patrol.

Make their behavior believable and lightweight.

Do not use complicated machine-learning systems.

Implement enemy behavior with efficient finite-state machines.

## 7. STEALTH SYSTEM

Allow the player to:
- Hide behind designated objects.
- Break enemy line of sight.
- Move away from detected enemies.
- Use a hide interaction button.

While hiding:
- Make the player visually less noticeable.
- Prevent movement only when the player is actively using a fixed hiding spot.
- Allow the player to leave hiding normally.

Enemies must not magically track invisible players.

## 8. LOOT AND INTERACTION

Place several collectible objects throughout the facility.

Include:
- Electronic components.
- Energy cells.
- Research documents.
- Rare technology modules.

Give each item:
- A recognizable 3D model.
- A name.
- A rarity.
- A pickup notification.

Use a small inventory with six slots.

Add interactive storage containers and computer terminals.

## 9. EXTRACTION

Create one clearly visible extraction point.

The player must collect at least three research items before extraction becomes available.

When the player reaches the extraction point:
- Display an interaction prompt.
- Start a short extraction countdown.
- Show extraction progress.
- Display a mission completion screen.

Show recovered items and earned credits.

## 10. USER INTERFACE

Create a polished dark sci-fi HUD.

Display:
- Health.
- Energy.
- Battery.
- Inventory capacity.
- Current objective.
- Interaction prompts.
- Extraction status.

Add a pause menu and mission completion screen.

Keep the interface readable on mobile screens.

## 11. AUDIO

If lightweight audio is available, include:
- Ambient laboratory sounds.
- Electronic interface sounds.
- Footsteps.
- Robot movement sounds.
- Warning signals.

Audio must be optional and must never prevent the game from running.

## 12. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

These requirements are critical:

- Target smooth performance on mid-range Android devices.
- Use low-poly geometry.
- Keep texture resolution small.
- Use a limited number of real-time lights.
- Avoid expensive post-processing.
- Avoid real-time global illumination.
- Use simple shadows or baked-looking lighting.
- Keep the number of active objects reasonable.
- Reuse geometry and materials.
- Use efficient collision detection.
- Avoid unnecessary background processing.
- Keep memory usage low.
- Include a graphics quality setting if practical.

Do not load large external assets.

Generate simple 3D models procedurally when necessary.

## 13. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Use a browser-compatible 3D engine.
- Prefer Three.js.
- Use WebGL.
- Make the game playable directly in the browser.
- Do not require external APIs or paid services.
- Do not require an account or server connection during gameplay.
- Make all controls functional.
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
- Organize files efficiently.
- Ensure the project builds successfully.

## 14. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITY

First create a working playable version containing:

1. A 3D environment.
2. A recognizable player character.
3. Third-person camera.
4. Responsive movement.
5. Collision detection.
6. Two working enemy robots.
7. Collectible objects.
8. A functional extraction point.
9. Mobile controls.

Only after these features work, improve visual details and animations.

Do not implement decorative features that do not work.

Do not create a large unfinished game.

The final result should be a compact, atmospheric and genuinely enjoyable 3D sci-fi game that demonstrates excellent visual quality without requiring powerful hardware.

Most importantly: BUILD A WORKING GAME, NOT JUST A BEAUTIFUL SCREENSHOT.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
